claim: Conducted and transcribed a qualitative user interview exploring dietary lapses, sugar cravings, and habit-building strategies.
detail: Analyzed the transcript across motivation, mental models, agency, coping, and social norms to identify incremental goal-setting as a coping strategy.

claim: Designed survey questions and an interactive research tool to capture participants' daily emotions around healthy habits.
detail: Iterated on the tool after an initial misalignment so participants could complete it with minimal explanation during interviews.

claim: On a team of five, prototyped Fit Anywhere, a lo-fi fitness app using incremental goal-setting, prompts, and feedback loops.
detail: Prioritized affordability, accountability, and motivation with progress tracking to support habit formation for adults aged 21–35.

claim: Designed a five-stage user journey map incorporating an empathy map to model motivations and barriers in healthy habit formation.
detail: Revisited interview data and repeated affinity mapping on a team of five to map stages from dedication through reflection on effort.

claim: Synthesized three peer-reviewed public health studies on how social and home environments shape diet and activity.
detail: Derived research questions and interview objectives examining workplace norms, financial barriers, food insecurity, and cultural traditions.

claim: On a team of five, authored a UX research plan with six hypotheses and a 45-minute interview guide for young adults.
detail: Mapped four stakeholder groups, targeted participants aged 21–35, and defined consent, privacy, and bias-mitigation protocols for food-insecurity interviews.

claim: On a team of five, synthesized interviews and surveys into behavioral themes covering social validation and self-perception.
detail: Defined a growth-mindset behavioral archetype and identified barriers including food costs, food deserts, impulsive snacking, and household influence.
